Answer: F
Reason: The chest X-rays show a well-circumscribed, solitary opacity in the anterior mediastinum/pleural space (marked by asterisks) without evidence of lymphadenopathy, bone destruction, or diffuse pleural thickening. This radiographic appearance, combined with the subacute symptoms of cough and chest pain, is most characteristic of a localized fibrous tumor of the pleura (solitary fibrous tumor), whereas lymphoma typically presents with bulky nodal disease and mesothelioma with diffuse pleural involvement.
